title: Inspect a lot with a two-limit gauge and release or hold it
instruction: Check each block, lying flat, with the two-bar gauge: put blocks that slide under the green GO bar but not under the red NO-GO bar in the green ACCEPT tray, blocks that don't fit under the GO bar in the red OVERSIZE tray, and blocks that also slide under the NO-GO bar in the blue UNDERSIZE tray; then put the yellow lot tag on the green RELEASE pad if at most 2 of the 6 blocks were out of tolerance, otherwise on the red HOLD pad.
context: Inspection decides a lot, not just its parts: each piece is gauged against both limits and sorted, then the count of rejects against the acceptance number releases or holds the whole lot. The three heights are 3.5 mm apart, too close to judge reliably by eye.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y left; heights from the table top (74.75 cm above the floor); sizes are length (x) x width (y) x height. Blocks: six bare machined aluminium blocks (silver-grey), numbered on the underside, lying flat with the long side along x; footprints 1, 6.4 x 4.4; 2, 6.0 x 4.2; 3, 5.4 x 4.1; 4, 5.6 x 4.1; 5, 5.6 x 4.0; 6, 5.5 x 4.0 cm; density 2.7 g/cm3. Heights by lot, blocks 1 to 6 (U 3.20, G 3.55, O 3.90 cm): A, U G O O U G; B, G U O G G G; C, O G U G O G. Places: a front row at x = 10 and a back row at x = 17.5, each at y = 8, 0 and -8. Lots (one per trial; block numbers by place, front row then back, left to right): A, 1 2 3 / 4 5 6; B, 2 3 1 / 5 6 4; C, 3 5 6 / 2 4 1. The screenshot shows A. Gauge: a fixed steel bridge, near face at x = 31, 2 cm deep; dark grey posts 2 x 2 cm at y = 12, 0 and -12; a green GO bar, 1 cm thick, from y = 1 to 13, underside 3.75 cm up; a red NO-GO bar from y = -13 to -1, underside 3.40 cm up; each over a 10 cm lane. Trays: fixed plastic, 1 cm walls 3 cm tall, 0.4 cm floor, centred at x = 30, 16 cm inside along x: a green ACCEPT tray at y = 18 to 36 inside; on the right one tray split by a 1 cm divider into a red OVERSIZE half (inside y = -15.5 to -26) and a blue UNDERSIZE half (inside y = -27 to -37.5). Lot tag: a yellow plastic cube, 3 cm, 30 g, at (10, 17). Lot pads: fixed plastic, 6 x 6 cm, 3 mm tall: green RELEASE centred at (10, 24), red HOLD centred at (17, 20.5).
scoring: Only the end state is scored, not the gauge passes. In a tray (or half): centre inside its walls, underside within 1.5 cm of its floor (so not stacked or on a wall), still (under 1 cm/s), and both fingertip centres 2 cm or more from the block; any orientation. Right tray: ACCEPT for 3.55 cm blocks (under GO, not under NO-GO), OVERSIZE for 3.90 cm, UNDERSIZE for 3.20 cm. Wrong: in any other tray, or off the table. Blocks anywhere else on the table, including one left under a bar, count neither way. Sort: 0.7 x (right - 3 x wrong) / 6, not below 0. Lot tag: on a pad when its centre is over the pad, its underside within 1 cm of it, still, and both fingertip centres 2 cm or more from it. The right pad is RELEASE with at most 2 of the 6 out of tolerance, otherwise HOLD. +0.3 with all six in their right trays and the tag on the right pad (1.0; the trial ends once this holds 1 s). The tag on the wrong pad caps the score at 0.2. So leaving everything, one tray for all, gauging with one bar, swapping OVERSIZE and UNDERSIZE, or the tag without the sort score 0. The task's score is the mean over one trial of each lot. On real arms, judge from a top-down photo after the arms withdraw, reading each block's number on its underside.
reset_notes: Put the six blocks back flat, long side along x, at the next layout's places (A, B, C in turn).
fidelity: Approximate. The limits are exaggerated: real gauges split hundredths of a millimetre; here the heights are 3.5 mm apart, a passing block clears its bar by 2 mm and a blocked one is 1.5 mm too tall, as tighter fits are unreliable in the simulator. The gauge and trays are fixed; three fixed lots, chosen at the start. The blocks are rigid uniform boxes; the simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), more than bare aluminium on steel.
